intended_object: The subspace A_F(D) + F of the repartition (adele) space A_F of an algebraic function field F/k, viewed as a k-subspace of A_F (Stichtenoth §I.5). The quotient A_F/(A_F(D)+F) gives the index of specialty i(D), and Weil differentials bounded by D vanish on this subspace. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The body takes the sum `adeleFiltration D ⊔ diagonalRepartitions k F` inside `Place k F → F`. Here `adeleFiltration D` is A_F(D) = {a | v_P(a_P) ≤ exp(D_P) for all P}, and `diagonalRepartitions k F` is the diagonal copy of F. The body then restricts this sum to A_F with `Submodule.submoduleOf`, which pulls it back along the inclusion A_F ↪ (Place → F). This gives (A_F(D) + F) ∩ A_F as a k-subspace of A_F.

When F/k is a function field, the file shows that A_F(D) + F ≤ A_F (`adeleFiltration_sup_diagonalRepartitions_le`). So the intersection is exactly Stichtenoth's subspace A_F(D) + F of A_F. Stating it as a subspace of A_F is what is needed to take the quotient A_F/(A_F(D)+F) and to define Weil differentials as k-linear forms on A_F.

The bounds are stated multiplicatively, v_P(a_P) ≤ exp(D_P). This correctly handles zero entries, which satisfy the bound at every place, so the definition has no junk-value problem.

The setting, an arbitrary field extension F/k with its places, is the natural one for this construction. Mathlib has no repartition spaces for function fields indexed by places, so there is no more general counterpart.
